records.name: Literacy Nation
records.summary: Helps independent authors and readers. It runs a yearly indie author book fair that is free to attend, offers free masterclasses, and gives awards for independent books.
records.what_you_do: Come to the free book fair, join a free masterclass, or ask about helping on a committee for events, marketing or fundraising.

schedule.text: Annual indie author book fair, listed for August 8, 2026. Masterclasses are free to register for on the website.

locations.label: Book fair venue, 4th District Container Village

cost.text: Book fair and masterclasses are free. Membership is $49 for 12 months. Authors and vendors pay a table fee ($50 for members, $125 for non-members).

first_step.how: Come to the free book fair on August 8, 2026, or register for a free masterclass on the website
first_step.basis: Fair admission and masterclass sign-up are free and open to the public, though the volunteer form link on the site was still a placeholder.

records.notes: The site uses the name LiteracyNation Inc. The IRS filing address (1125 N 65th St) does not appear on the website, so it is not published here. The volunteer form link on the site is a placeholder. No exact interest tag exists for indie author support; zines_media is the closest fit.

records.name: Lotus Behavioral Health and Rehabilitative Services
records.notes: A clinical behavioral health provider that takes clients for therapy and case management. It is not a community program. The website shows only a Baltimore, MD office and a 2020 copyright, with no dated items. The IRS record lists a Philadelphia address, which the website does not mention. Also a business with no community program, so it would be out of scope even if it served Philadelphia.

records.name: NorthStar of GIS
records.summary: Works for racial justice in mapping and GIS, aiming to bring more Black people into geospatial careers through mentorship, scholarships and events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer or join a committee through the website, register for the annual conference, or take part in its mentorship and events.

schedule.text: Annual conference (the 2025 edition was November 19 to 20 at Howard University in Washington, D.C.), plus events and volunteer sign-ups listed on the website.

locations.label: Mailing address listed on the website

cost.text: Costs are not listed on the website.

first_step.how: Sign up on the volunteer page of the website, or register for the next annual conference through the Events page
first_step.basis: Volunteering and conference registration are listed publicly on the website, and no application is shown.

records.notes: A global movement with a Philadelphia mailing address on its site. The 2026 conference theme is announced but no 2026 date was shown. The mission centers Black people in geospatial fields, but the site does not limit who may join, so community is left empty. Closest tags: racial_equity for the mission, digital_skills for the GIS focus.

records.name: Philadelphia Community Development Corporation of Alliances
records.summary: Raises money for a health clinic and for homeless outreach, and asks people to get involved by getting in touch.
records.what_you_do: Contact the group by email or phone to ask how to help with its clinic or homeless outreach, or to make a donation.

schedule.text: No dates are shown on the website. Ask the group for current clinic and outreach days.

first_step.how: Email pcdcoa@gmail.com or call 267-702-6159 and ask how to help with the clinic or outreach
first_step.basis: The site invites people to get in touch, but it does not say what volunteering involves or when it happens.

records.notes: The site shows a 2021 copyright and an Upcoming Events link with no dated events, so the status rests on a working site with no dates. The site does not name a service area, and the IRS filing address in Philadelphia is not shown on the site. Owner should confirm the Philadelphia service area before this goes live. The site also lists the group as established in 2000.

records.name: More Pass Plus Learning Center
records.summary: Offers workshops, training and resources to parents, caregivers and families, with a focus on learning, faith and family life.
records.what_you_do: Attend a workshop or training, or send the contact form to ask about upcoming sessions and how to get involved.

schedule.text: Workshops and trainings are announced on the website without dates. Ask the group for the next session.

first_step.how: Send the contact form on morepassplus.com, or email morepassplus3@gmail.com, to ask about the next workshop
first_step.basis: Anyone can reach the group by the contact form, email or phone, and no membership or application is mentioned.

records.notes: The site gives no street address and does not name a service area. The IRS list has a Philadelphia address (19131). Owner should confirm the Philadelphia service area before this goes live. The only dated item on the site is a default WordPress placeholder post, so it is not used as evidence. No exact tag exists for parent workshops; school_parent_groups is the closest fit.

notes: Budget: both WebSearch calls used (on the Racial Justice Organizing Committee and the Center for Civic Leadership and Change); no further searches. 28 fetches used. Verdicts: 12 publish (8 of these are unknown and held back because nothing was found beyond IRS data, 4 are publish with low confidence), 3 out_of_area (Lotus, CSEIA, Umbrella of Ukrainian Hope), 0 hide, 0 not_a_group, 0 duplicate. Groups with no working website (Love Is the Key, Mama Sophia, Strong Families, Queens United, Ryan Family Hope, One Vision One Purpose, Racial Justice Organizing Committee, Center for Civic Leadership and Change) were checked on ProPublica by EIN as a public IRS source; most IRS summaries have no mission text. Two of these (Racial Justice Organizing Committee and Center for Civic Leadership and Change) were the only ones that got a web search. Several candidates (Mama Sophia, Love Is the Key, Strong Families, Queens United, Ryan Family Hope, One Vision One Purpose) got no search because the budget was spent. Fix next: a person could check Racial Justice Organizing Committee, Center for Civic Leadership and Change, and the four unknown IRS groups by hand. Owner decisions needed: whether CSEIA and Umbrella of Ukrainian Hope should count as out of area, and whether PCDC of Alliances and More Pass Plus should go live without a stated Philadelphia service area.
